text:
sam: Quick sanity probe comparing SXM (NVLink) vs PCIe boards across our 4-GPU inference sharded runs. goal: steady-state p50/p95 + KV-cache cross-GPU transfer overhead. model: opt-6.7b, int8 quant, seq=1024.

jin: good — what exact command/config?

sam: ran this locally on raptor-2 nodes (same kernel/drivers). basic runner: 
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 numactl --physcpubind=0-31 --membind=0 ./run_infer \  --model opt-6.7b --quant int8 --batch 1,8,16 --seq 1024 --kernel auto --nvlink on
```

sam: key differences: SXM shows much lower cross-GPU latency and higher tok/s. numbers (median of 3 runs):
- SXM NVLink: batch=1 p50=48ms p95=63ms throughput~520 tok/s
- PCIe: batch=1 p50=72ms p95=110ms throughput~320 tok/s
- Cross-GPU KV transfer extra cost: PCIe added ~8-12ms tail, SXM ~1-2ms.

marie: did the runtime pick different kernels between platforms?

sam: yes — interesting bit in the logs: on SXM runtime chose fused attention kernel, on PCIe it fell back to block_attention. snippets: 
```
[info] kernel selector: fused_attn selected (bandwidth heuristic passed)
[warn] kernel selector: fallback -> block_attn (nvlink_bw insufficient for fused pipeline)
```

jin: which cuBLAS/cuDNN? driver?

sam: CUDA 12.1 + cuBLAS 12.1 patched. drivers identical. heuristic in our kernel selector looks at measured p2p_bw and decides whether kv-cache prefetch + fused pipeline is safe; PCIe numbers under threshold.

marta: CPU/NUMA pinning? that often bites us on PCIe.

sam: yep. default run had membind=0 (all memory on socket 0). when I force per-gpu local memory binding (numactl --membind mapped per GPU socket) PCIe p95 improved ~10ms. examples: 
```
# poor: all mem on socket0 -> hurts remote-GPU dma
numactl --membind=0 ./run_infer ...
# better: pin to local sockets (pseudo)
numactl --membind=0,2 ./run_infer --gpu-map 0:0,1:1,2:2,3:3 ...
```

sam: also toggled GDR (cuda_p2p and enabling peer access). enabling GDR/P2P reduced PCIe extra cost by ~6ms. still not as low as NVLink but much better.

jin: did you try forcing fused_attn on PCIe to measure correctness/perf tradeoff?

sam: forced it with --kernel fused_attn_force. result: some runs crash OOM on PCIe for batch>8 (fused needs more temporary memory), and p95 actually regressed due to extra stall/retries. safe to say fused is bandwidth-sensitive and mem-sensitive.

marie: any perf counters or nvidia topo output?

sam: pulled topo and p2p bw: 
```
# nvidia-smi topo --matrix (abridged)
GPU0    GPU1    GPU2    GPU3
GPU0   X       NVLINK  PCIE    PCIE
GPU1   NVLINK  X       PCIE    PCIE
GPU2   PCIE    PCIE    X       NVLINK
GPU3   PCIe    PCIe    NVLINK  X
```
measured p2p bw (iperf-like): SXM peer avg ~180 GB/s, PCIe peer avg ~20-40 GB/s depending crossbar.

marta: any region/cloud differences? like Naples vs Seoul racks?

sam: replicated on two regions. same relative delta. QE: if your workload shards heavily (kv sharing every token), SXM wins big. if you can partition to avoid cross-GPU traffic (replicate model or cache prefixes locally) PCIe can be acceptable with careful pinning and GDR.

ciara-bot: :chart_with_upwards_trend: summary note created in /perf/bench-notes (auto).

sam: TL;DR:
- SXM (NVLink) gives much lower tail latency and higher throughput for sharded KV workloads.
- PCIe can approach SXM only with: per-gpu NUMA-aware memory binding, GDR enabled, and sometimes manual kernel overrides — but stability/oom risk rises.
- Kernel selector heuristics should consider measured p2p_bw at runtime (we should persist a short p2p probe at startup).

jin: +1 on runtime p2p probe. can open an ops ticket to add it.

marie: can you drop logs and the exact runner flags into the bench doc? will add to onboarding checklist.

sam: will upload raw logs and CSV numbers to the bench doc later today. thanks. :thumbsup:
